pages.text: The curtains slid open. The mats grew bright. "Mio, nap time is over. Let us get up." Teacher Bau of Rainbow Class offered a hand. Mio pulled the blanket to their chin.

"I will get up myself." Mio, who wanted to do everything alone, pushed the hand away. "I will choose the biggest bread for snack. Just a little later." Gripping the purple bag straps against their chest, Mio lay down again.
Impatient Bobo stretched arms high on the mat. Beside Bobo, and farther along, more arms stretched. Only Mio stayed under a blanket. "A little more..." Those eyes closed again.
On opening their eyes, Mio found the mats empty. Only Mio's blanket remained. "Oh? Where is everyone?"
Mio's bread sat alone on the window table. It felt cold and hard. "We saved yours," Bobo said with an empty plate. Mio closed their mouth tightly.
Teacher Bau knelt beside the mat. "Getting up is not hard. When the curtains open, stretch your body long." Teacher Bau held Mio's hands, and together they reached up.
Arms stretch, legs stretch—sleepiness slipped away. "Oh? I am wide awake! Curtains open—stretch, stretch!" Mio's eyes sparkled brightly.
"After stretching, wash your face with cold water," Teacher Bau said. At the wash area, Mio cupped water in both hands and splashed their cheeks. Cool cheeks made those ears perk up.

After the next nap, Mio sat up before the curtains opened. Stretching one arm high, Mio showed three fingers. "One, curtains open—stretch, stretch! Two, feet on the floor! Three, wash with cold water!"
Teacher Bau sat Mio on a lap and patted their back. "Those who get up get warm bread." Stretching chased sleep away. Reaching both arms high, Mio called, "Curtains open—stretch, stretch!"
